priceSnapshot.note: TIMING DISCLOSURE FIRST. This is the END-DAY session for 20 September. Its nominal slot is 19:30 COT; it executed at 00:02 COT on 21 September, roughly four and a half hours late, and - this is the part that conditions the whole file - only ELEVEN MINUTES after the midday session, which was itself eleven hours late. The entire 20 September schedule collapsed into a twelve-minute window at the end of the day. Two consequences follow and both are honoured below. First, almost nothing can have changed since the midday file: price is 81,398.9 against 81,483.5, a move of minus 84.6 points or 0.10 percent, comfortably inside the 231.23-point 15m ATR14. Every figure here was nevertheless re-read from the source rather than copied forward, and where a number moved it is stated. Second, the OVERNIGHT GAP this file normally guards is not the usual six and a half hours - the midnight session is due at roughly 02:00 COT, under two hours away. That materially changes the stop-order calculus and is argued explicitly in overnightRisk. The Bogota trading day 20 September ran 80,173.5 to 82,099.0, a 1,925.5-point range, and closes with price in the upper third of it.

The one genuinely NEW read is in the liquidation tape and it is constructive: the fresh fills - everything since roughly 04:00 UTC, including the newest at 04:57:06 UTC - are SHORT liquidations clustered at 81,250 to 81,500, 86,337.24 USD of them, while the heavy long-liquidation weight at 81,000 and 80,750 is now over three hours old and fully reclaimed. overnightRisk: The gap this file is guarding is under two hours, not the usual six and a half. The midnight session is due at roughly 02:00 COT on 21 September and this report is being written at 00:02 COT, so the exposure window is about 118 minutes of Asian pre-session tape on a Sunday night rolling into Monday. That single fact drives the stop decision, and it is worth being explicit about the reasoning chain because it inverts this file's usual endday posture. Three tests, all of which have to point the same way before a resting stop earns its place. TEST ONE - is price near the reduce level? No. Spot is 81,398.9 and the gate is 80,750.0, a distance of 648.9 points or 1.57 times the 412.43-point 1H ATR14. The skill's own trigger is proximity to the reduce level and price is not close to it. TEST TWO - what does the most recent evidence say about resting stops here? It says they have been actively harmful. Friday's endday set a recommended stop at 80,568.6, 1.47 times the 1H ATR at the time. It filled near 80,133.4, an overshoot of 435.2 points, and price then recovered roughly 1,350 points within three hours; that level is now 914.9 points onside and the trade was a pure donation. The lesson logged eleven minutes ago reads that a resting stop placed inside the day's own noise is worse than no stop at all, and honouring a lesson the same night it is written is the whole point of writing it. TEST THREE - is there a liquidation magnet below into thin liquidity that would make a gap self-reinforcing? No, and this is the strongest argument of the three. The 81,000 shelf carries 528,391.39 USD of purely long liquidations and the 80,750 shelf another 140,760.20 USD, but both were created during the 01:15 to 01:45 UTC flush to 80,133.4, over three hours ago, and every settled hour since 02:00 UTC has closed above 80,990. Spent fuel is a floor, not a magnet. Meanwhile the fresh end of the tape - 86,337.24 USD across the 81,250 and 81,500 buckets, newest fill 04:57:06 UTC at 81,417.4 - is entirely SHORT liquidations printing at and just above spot. The pressure that is actually live right now points up, not down. All three tests fail, so stopOrder.recommended is FALSE and the overnight protection is the 80,750.0 settled-close gate handed to the midnight session instead. Now the catalysts, because no stop does not mean no risk. First and largest: this is the Sunday-night-into-Monday handover, the thinnest liquidity of the crypto week, and the 15m ATR14 at 231.23 has been expanding while the 4H at 810.53 and 1H at 412.43 compress - a coiled structure with a whipping fast frame is exactly the configuration that produces a violent, meaningless 300-point spike into Asian hours. Second: the US 10-year sits at 5.00 percent and the Monday cash open is the first chance for that to transmit into risk assets; QQQ closed Friday at its own 21-session high with the 52-week high 3.63 percent away, so the equity sleeve is extended into a yield level that has not been friendly. Third: the next US spot Bitcoin ETF print lands Monday 21 September after the cash close, and the two-day plus 592.5 million USD streak - including Farside's upward revision of the 18 September figure from 322.3 to 433.0 million - is now priced in; a negative Monday print would remove the clearest fundamental support this move has. Fourth and most specific: the unresolved 1H bearish divergence at 82,099.0 is a live short-side invitation, and if Asian tape probes that high again and fails a second time, the rejection will be faster and deeper than the first because the shorts liquidated in the last hour will have been replaced by better-placed ones. The midnight session inherits 51.19 USDT of cash precisely so it can act on whichever of these resolves.

liquidation.note: 528,391.39 USD across 54 fills, ALL of them long liquidations, zero shorts - re-verified this session against the midday reading of 535,136 USD, the small difference being the 100-fill sample window rolling forward. This is the shelf that broke during the 01:15 to 01:45 UTC flush from 82,099.0 to 80,857.6, and the operative word remains BROKE. The fuel was burned, not banked. Price reclaimed the area within two hours and every settled hour since 02:00 UTC has closed above 80,990. It is now over three hours old. Kept flagged as the extreme-intensity magnet because it is still the single heaviest structure on the tape and a re-break would matter enormously, but as of tonight it functions as the floor of the scalp box rather than a downside target.

140,760.20 USD across 14 fills, again purely long liquidations with zero shorts, unchanged from the midday reading. Same 01:51 to 02:00 UTC window, same one-sided character, same three-hour age. This is where the reduce gate sits and the coincidence is deliberate: a settled 1H close back below this shelf would mean the reclaim failed and the burned fuel was relit, which is the one sequence that turns tonight's bullish structure into a genuine breakdown.

THE ONLY GENUINELY NEW DATA IN THIS REPORT. 86,337.24 USD of SHORT liquidations against just 513.31 USD of longs, 27 fills, and critically these are the FRESH end of the tape - the newest fill on the entire feed is 04:57:06 UTC at 81,417.4 and it is a short being taken out, five minutes before this report was written. The midday file read this band as 86,850 USD without splitting the side; the split is what matters. Over the last hour the squeeze has quietly reversed direction: the heavy long-liquidation weight below is stale and reclaimed, while shorts are being stopped out at and just above spot right now. That is a constructive read, and it is the reason the bullish tilt survives a session in which price fell 84.6 points.

calibration.note: An eleven-minute review window, which is not long enough to grade anything, and the honest thing is to say so rather than manufacture a verdict. Neither of the midday gates fired. The reduce gate at 80,750.0 was never approached - the low since the midday snapshot is 81,385.0, leaving 635.0 points of clearance. The add gate at 82,099.0 was never approached either; the only settled 1H close in the window was 81,404.1, short by 694.9 points. So priorReduceFired is FALSE and the add gate is equally unmet. The 77,167.3 invalidation held with 4,231.6 points of clearance, its fifth consecutive session and still its widest margin of the series. actingHelped is deliberately NULL rather than false: the midday session bought 20 USDT of spot core at 81,483.5 and the mark is now 81,398.9, so the position is 84.6 points or 0.10 percent offside - but 0.10 percent inside eleven minutes, against a 15m ATR of 231.23, is indistinguishable from noise and grading it either way would be dishonest. The midnight session, roughly two hours out, is the first run with a defensible window in which to judge it. What this file WILL stand behind is the stop-order call. Friday's endday recommended a resting stop at 80,568.6, it filled near 80,133.4 and price recovered about 1,350 points; that lesson was logged eleven minutes ago and tonight's file declines to repeat it, with the reasoning laid out test by test in overnightRisk. Declining to set a stop two hours before the next session is not complacency, it is the first application of a lesson this desk paid for in cash.
